title: Ratification of the 19th Amendment
summary: On 18 August 1920 Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment, supplying the three-fourths of states needed. The amendment, passed by Congress in 1919, guarantees American women the right to vote. Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified the ratification on 26 August 1920.

uncertainty.note: Ratification by Tennessee on 18 August 1920; certification by the Secretary of State on 26 August 1920.

as_recorded.value: On August 18, 1920, Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the amendment
Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified the ratification on August 26, 1920

importance.justification: The National Archives says the amendment legally guarantees American women the right to vote.

related.because: The Tennessee State Library and Archives says the roots of the women's suffrage effort are traced to the 1848 Seneca Falls Convention.
